{"path":"effect_gouraud_shaded_cube_openrouter-moonshotai-kimi-k3_01.html","edit_description":"Create a NEW single self-contained HTML file (no external libraries, no WebGL — Canvas 2D only) implementing a realtime Gouraud-shaded rotating cube with a software rasterizer. Full spec below — implement ALL of it in vanilla inline JavaScript.

PAGE STRUCTURE:
- <!DOCTYPE html>, <html>, <head> with <meta charset="utf-8">, <title>Gouraud Shaded Cube</title>, inline <style>: html/body margin 0, padding 0, overflow hidden, background #05060a; canvas display block. 
- A single fullscreen <canvas id="c">. All HUD text is drawn onto the canvas with fillText (no DOM overlays needed, though a tiny hint line is fine to draw on canvas).
- One inline <script> at the end of body. Everything in an IIFE or top-level script.

RENDERING ARCHITECTURE (Canvas 2D only):
- Main canvas sized to window (resize handler updates it).
- An offscreen canvas (document.createElement('canvas')) at REDUCED resolution for software rasterization: buffer width/height = main canvas size divided by a downscale factor (use ~2, i.e. half resolution, min 1) — recompute on resize. Get its ImageData once per resize.
- Each frame: clear the ImageData pixel array by copying a pre-built background template (a Uint8ClampedArray filled once per resize with opaque dark color, e.g. rgba(10,12,20,255), via pixels.set(bgTemplate)), rasterize the cube's triangles into it, putImageData to the offscreen canvas, then on the main canvas: set imageSmoothingEnabled = true and drawImage(offscreen, 0, 0, mainW, mainH) so the buffer is upscaled smoothly to fullscreen.

3D PIPELINE:
- Cube geometry: 8 vertices at (±1, ±1, ±1). 6 quad faces with consistent counter-clockwise winding when viewed from OUTSIDE. Each quad split into 2 triangles → 12 triangles total, stored as index triples. Give each face a distinct base color (e.g. red, green, blue, yellow, magenta, cyan — as {r,g,b} 0-255); both triangles of a quad share the face color.
- Per-vertex normals for Gouraud: for a cube centered at origin use the normalized vertex position as the vertex normal (equals the average of the three adjacent face normals) — this yields smooth color interpolation across faces.
- Animation time t (seconds, advanced by dt each frame unless paused). Rotation angles: ax = t*0.7, ay = t*1.0 (optionally az = t*0.35). Build standard 3D rotation matrices rotX(ax), rotY(ay) (and rotZ if used) as 3x3 arrays or inline formulas; transform every vertex and every vertex normal by the combined rotation (normals rotate the same way — rotation is orthonormal so no renormalization issues, but renormalize anyway for safety).
- Camera: after rotation, translate vertices along +Z by a camera distance (e.g. z += 4.5). Lighting is computed in WORLD space (after rotation, BEFORE the z-translation).
- Moving light source: a point light orbiting the cube, e.g. lightPos = (3.0*cos(t*0.9), 2.2*sin(t*0.6), 3.0*sin(t*0.9)). 
- Per-vertex Lambert lighting: for each vertex, L = normalize(lightPos - worldVertexPos); intensity = ambient + diffuse * max(0, dot(worldNormal, L)) with ambient ≈ 0.18, diffuse ≈ 0.9. Vertex color (per triangle corner) = faceBaseColor * intensity, clamped to 255. Store the lit color on each triangle corner.
- Perspective projection: focal = (bufferHeight * 1.1) (or similar); for each camera-space vertex: sx = bufferW/2 + x * focal / z; sy = bufferH/2 - y * focal / z. Skip/guard z <= 0.1.
- Backface culling: per triangle, in CAMERA space (after z-translation), compute edge1 = v1-v0, edge2 = v2-v0, normal = cross(edge1, edge2); viewDir = v0 (vector from camera at origin to the triangle); if dot(normal, viewDir) >= 0 the triangle faces away → cull it. (Winding must be consistent with this test; if the cube renders inside-out, flip the comparison or the winding — verify logically: outward-facing triangles have dot(normal, viewDir) < 0.)

GOURAUD RASTERIZER (the core requirement — real per-pixel color interpolation, NOT canvas gradients):
- Implement a scanline triangle rasterizer function fillTriangle(p0, p1, p2) where each p has screen x, y and rgb color (r0,g0,b0 etc. as floats).
- Standard algorithm: sort the 3 vertices by y; handle flat-bottom and flat-top halves (or the generic split-at-middle-y approach). For each scanline y (integer, clamped to [0, bufferH-1]): interpolate x and r,g,b along the two active edges by the vertical fraction, then walk the span from xLeft to xRight (clamped to [0, bufferW-1]) interpolating r,g,b linearly across the span, writing each pixel into the ImageData array at index (y*bufferW + x)*4 with alpha 255. Guard against division by zero (degenerate/zero-height triangles). Use local variables and typed-array writes for speed; no per-pixel function calls.
- Because the cube is convex and backface-culled, no z-buffer is needed (front faces never overlap).

WIREFRAME MODE:
- Boolean wireframe, toggled by pressing W (keydown listener, check e.key.toLowerCase() === 'w'). When ON: skip the ImageData rasterization entirely (still clear main canvas with the dark background via fillRect), and stroke each non-culled triangle's 3 edges on the MAIN canvas with ctx.strokeStyle a bright color (e.g. #7CFC98 or white), lineWidth ~1.5, mapping buffer screen coords up to main canvas coords (multiply by the downscale factor). When OFF: normal Gouraud path. Show current mode in the HUD.

PAUSE:
- Boolean paused, toggled by P (e.key.toLowerCase() === 'p'). When paused: do NOT advance t (freeze rotation and light) but keep rendering every frame so toggling wireframe still updates the view. Show "PAUSED" in the HUD when active.

FPS DISPLAY:
- Measure real frame dt via performance.now() deltas; maintain a smoothed FPS (exponential moving average, e.g. fps = fps*0.9 + (1/dt)*0.1). Draw with fillText in a corner: "FPS: 60" (rounded), plus a second line: "W: wireframe (off) | P: pause" style status, and optionally "Gouraud shading — Canvas 2D software rasterizer". Use a monospace font ~14px, light color with slight shadow or dark outline for readability.

LIGHT INDICATOR (nice touch, keep it simple): project the light position (rotated? no — light is world space; apply the same z-translation then project) and draw a small filled yellow/white circle with a soft glow (radial gradient is allowed for this sprite only, or just two concentric circles) at its main-canvas position, in both modes.

MAIN LOOP:
- requestAnimationFrame loop; dt = clamp((now - last)/1000, 0, 0.05); if (!paused) t += dt; then per frame: rotate vertices+normals, compute lighting per vertex per face corner, translate z, project, cull, then either rasterize to buffer + blit (shaded mode) or stroke edges (wireframe mode), draw light indicator + HUD text.

QUALITY BAR:
- Clean, commented, organized code with section comments (// ---- Math ----, // ---- Geometry ----, // ---- Rasterizer ----, etc.). No external requests of any kind. Must run by double-clicking the file. No frameworks, no WebGL, no OffscreenCanvas API (use a regular detached canvas). Avoid allocations in the hot loop where practical (preallocate the rotated/projected vertex arrays).
- The visual result: a smoothly rotating cube with visibly smooth color gradients across each face (darker away from the orbiting light, bright near it), correct hidden-face removal, ~60 FPS shown in the HUD.

Write the complete file."}
